citation: Bakkensen et al. (2017), Validating Resilience and Vulnerability Indices in the Context of Natural Disasters
purpose_of_ranking: Guide disaster preparation, recovery and adaptation decisions using resilience/vulnerability indices
validation_same_period_or_later_period: Observed historical outcomes; later/non-overlapping timing unclear from abstract/metadata
geographic_holdout_used: No/unclear; regional validation, not held-out geography from available text
human_impact_outcome_used: Yes - fatalities; also losses and disaster declarations
main_contribution: Empirically validates five disaster resilience/vulnerability indices against observed outcomes and shows indices differ by outcome.
direct_overlap_with_our_study: High conceptual overlap: external validation of disaster indices using observed outcomes.
important_difference_from_our_study: Not India-specific, not flood-only district prioritisation, no verified satellite validation, no verified future temporal holdout or simple historical baseline comparison.
threat_to_novelty: Medium-high: establishes external validation of disaster indices but not our complete design.
evidence_source_page_or_section: Wiley abstract/RePEc abstract: observed losses, fatalities and declarations; five indices; southeastern US.
examines_whether_complexity_adds_value: Partly - compares multiple established indices, but not fitted complexity vs simple indicators from available text

citation: Tellman et al. (2020), Using Disaster Outcomes to Validate Components of Social Vulnerability to Floods
purpose_of_ranking: Validate vulnerability indicators/components for directing flood-death and damage reduction
creates_composite_index: No - compares SoVI, individual socioeconomic variables and flood-intensity-only models
outcome_index_claims_to_represent: Social vulnerability to flood deaths and property damage
validation_same_period_or_later_period: Same historical event period, 2008-2012, from available abstract
predictor_and_outcome_periods_overlap: Yes or unclear; no non-overlapping future holdout verified
satellite_data_used: No - stream gauge flood intensity control from verified abstract
human_impact_outcome_used: Yes - flood deaths; property damage also
simple_baseline_compared: Yes - flood intensity variables only, but not event-count ranking
fitted_model_compared_with_simple_indica: Yes - individual variables and SoVI versus flood-intensity-only model
reporting_bias_discussed: Data limitations noted generally; temporal reporting drift not verified
main_contribution: Uses flood outcomes to validate social vulnerability components and shows outcome-specific variables can outperform generic SoVI.
direct_overlap_with_our_study: Very high conceptual overlap: flood-specific observed human outcomes, model-vs-index comparison and outcome-specific validation.
important_difference_from_our_study: US, not India; county/event regression rather than district priority ranking; no satellite inundation validation; no strict future non-overlapping temporal validation verified; no state-block uncertainty verified.
threat_to_novelty: High for broad claims about outcome-specific validation; moderate for our India temporal/satellite/simple-ranking combination.
evidence_source_page_or_section: DigitalCommons abstract lines: compares socioeconomic variables, SoVI and flood intensity only; 11,629 events; death/damage outcomes.
full_text_confidence_level: Open abstract and repository metadata; full PDF not accessible through tool
tests_physical_burden_and_later_human_im: No - tests same-period flood intensity/human outcomes, not satellite physical burden plus later impacts
